title: Coverage Theater (Chasing Statement Metrics)
pattern: Tests written solely to satisfy a strict percentage requirement of statement coverage, exercising trivial methods (like simple accessors, getters, setters) without meaningful asserts or logical checks.
why_bad: Statement coverage is a blunt metric that does not guarantee correctness [7, 512]. It incentivizes "coverage theater" where developers write low-value tests for boilerplate code [513], which then become a maintenance drag when schemas or types change [671].
detection: Tests with zero assertions, or testing auto-generated boilerplate, accessors, and compilers. High suite coverage metrics (~100%) but poor assertions or zero mutation validation [417].
counterexample: `Context-dependent`. Standard basic coverage tracking is fine, but treating coverage as a target rather than a diagnostic tool is a smell [513].
fix: Prioritize test completeness over raw line coverage; use mutation testing tools to verify that tests actually fail when logic is altered, and stop testing compiler-guaranteed accessors [29, 671].
source:
*   *Composing Software*, "What is test coverage?" (p. 207-208) [3, 7, 375]
*   *Software Engineering at Google*, "A Note on Code Coverage" (p. 222) [512, 513]
*   *Fundamentals of Software Architecture*, "Modularity / Testability" (p. 47) [417]
*   *The Art of Readable Code*, "Going Too Far: Coverage" (p. 151) [671]
